tagline.text: A Marian shrine in Parañaque known for Wednesday devotion, mosaics and a spacious nave

location.label: Location
location.text: Redemptorist Road, Baclaran, Parañaque, Metro Manila

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Check daily worship and access notices year-round; avoid service peaks for a quieter visit

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: 1–2 hours or a half-day with a service

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱600–1,200 per person as a planning budget for city transport, food and contingency; flights and lodging excluded

children.text: Baclaran Church, the National Shrine of Our Mother of Perpetual Help in Parañaque, combines Wednesday devotion with a spacious nave, rose window, mosaics and memorial spaces. Plan around actual services and access notices, and confirm any special tower or gallery entry separately.

Baclaran Church is the National Shrine of Our Mother of Perpetual Help in Parañaque, Metro Manila. The familiar names Baclaran Church and Redemptorist Church refer to the same shrine. Busy roads and shops give way to a long nave and tree-lined approaches inside the grounds. It is best understood as a place of ongoing prayer and everyday visits, rather than a building to photograph quickly. Visitors can explore respectfully around the services and local instructions in progress.

The shrine’s own history describes the Redemptorists’ move to Baclaran in 1932 and the growth of Wednesday devotion after the local introduction of the Perpetual Novena in 1948. The present church dates from the 1950s. Its architectural guide credits Cesar Concio and Jesse Bontoc with a Modern Romanesque design. Looking at the rose window, rounded entrances and long ceiling in sequence helps connect the strong exterior with the light and scale of the interior.

In June 2026 the shrine and the University of Santo Tomas signed an agreement to prepare a Conservation Management Plan. This concerns research and planning, and does not establish that every restoration project is complete or every visitor area is continuously open. Check worship schedules on the official site and ask the shrine about access to areas such as the bell tower and gallery. The gallery’s photograph of a 2016 art exhibition is an archival event record, not a promise that those works remain on display.
Study the broad front and repeated rounded arches before locating the rose window above the entrance. Keep the steps and doorways clear for worshippers when taking a photograph.
The shrine relates the ceiling design to hands in prayer. From an available seat, notice the depth and light toward the sanctuary; limit sightseeing movement during services.

View the Our Mother of Perpetual Help icon, the focus of devotion here, from a permitted position. Distinguish the original image’s history in Rome from the icon venerated at Baclaran, using the shrine’s interpretation.

The official timetable lists several Wednesday novena services, Masses and benedictions. Their language and form vary. Choose a particular service if attending, and respect seating and circulation even when observing quietly.

Mosaic walls and the monument to the disappeared offer a quieter way to explore the grounds. Focus on the works and interpretation rather than photographing people who are praying or remembering relatives.

The architectural guide describes a detached tower built in 2015 with 24 Austrian bells. Viewing it from outside differs from entering it: special access on an operator’s heritage tour does not establish unrestricted public entry.

For a first visit without attending a service, allow roughly one to two hours as a planning suggestion. Services, queues and heat may make a shorter visit or a longer break more suitable. If attending Mass or a novena, choose that session first and place sightseeing around it. There is no need to fill a day with consecutive Wednesday services.
Confirm the shrine name and your return station, read local notices, then view the façade and rose window without blocking foot traffic.
Check whether a service is underway, enter from a suitable side and sit briefly. Observe the ceiling and sanctuary without entering restricted areas.
Rest in the shade and look at mosaics and memorials. Ask staff about gallery or tower access if interested, and finish with the ordinary visit if those areas are unavailable.
Check return transport before crowds grow. Allow separate travel time for another stop and verify evening services and last trains rather than assuming availability.

The address is Redemptorist Road, Baclaran, Parañaque City. The representative coordinates, 14.5314, 120.9952, were checked against Wikipedia’s map and the same building in OpenStreetMap. They locate the church, not an approved vehicle stop or a currently open gate. Distinguish Baclaran station in Pasay from the shrine in Parañaque and check the full name to avoid another similarly named Marian church.

Redemptorist–Aseana is an LRT-1 access station for the shrine, also used by the operator’s heritage tour. It is separate from Baclaran station. Check the line map and exits and use designated crossings such as footbridges. Gate positions, works and crowds can make the actual walking route longer than the apparent map distance.

items.title: By car or from the airport

children.text: From Ninoy Aquino International Airport, use the designated pickup area for your terminal and confirm the shrine’s full name. Its location in the airport area does not guarantee a short trip; congestion and terminal access vary. On busy Wednesdays, agree with the driver on legal drop-off and pickup points, and distinguish informal parking offers from official shrine instructions.

Plan indoor worship and a walk around the grounds against the day’s actual schedule throughout the year. Outdoor approaches and the walk to the station include exposure to sun and rain, so bring water and a small umbrella. For quieter architectural viewing, consider avoiding peaks around Wednesday devotions and Sunday Mass. If the service itself is your reason to visit, choose its published language and session, without assuming a quiet setting or available seat.

children.text: This research did not establish a tourist admission charge for an ordinary church visit. Donations, offerings and candle purchases should be understood separately from admission, following official local instructions. The figures below are editorial planning allowances for one person making a short visit from Metro Manila, not a shrine tariff. They exclude flights, accommodation, a full-day private car and separately booked heritage tours.

children.text: Confirm tower and gallery booking, charges and access separately. Special entry advertised on a previous tour does not establish free or continuous public access.

The shrine usually fits a half-day trip from accommodation already chosen for a Manila stay. If combining it with an airport arrival or departure, keep a generous flight buffer and do not assume the church can store large bags. When choosing accommodation, compare the actual walk to a station, late-return transport and noise comments in recent reviews. A short straight-line distance does not by itself establish a convenient walking route.

Food and drinks are available in the surrounding commercial area, but check the actual opening and cleanliness of any outlet. Keep meals out of worship spaces and take a water break in a permitted area before becoming exhausted. Old photographs of exhibitions or cafés do not establish that the same businesses operate today. If adding food or shopping, allow for crowds spilling into the streets around service times.

If the front entrance is crowded, ask staff which line is for a service and which route allows ordinary entry. Share the name of your return station with companions so that the group does not split between Baclaran and Redemptorist–Aseana stations.

The official site distinguishes Wednesday novena services, Masses and benedictions, including their language. Read the type of your chosen session rather than treating them all as Mass; special feasts may alter the timetable.
Avoid moving toward the altar for photographs or repeatedly crossing seating during prayer. Sightseeing shares the space with worship, so follow staff instructions about photography.

Distinguish an organized heritage tour from an ordinary individual visit. If the tower or gallery is essential, confirm the date, guide, price and stair requirements with the shrine or an active organizer before booking.

Photographs span different years: the 2016 exhibition is archival, the 2013 plaque records a historical notice, and the 2026 station image illustrates access. They do not establish today’s entire layout or exhibition arrangement.

On crowded days, agree on a meeting point and keep belongings close. If someone requests money for donations, prayers or parking, verify the arrangement with shrine staff or an official desk before paying. These are ordinary precautions for a busy urban religious site, rather than a claim about a particular incident. With children or companions with limited mobility, plan breaks before adding consecutive services.

Use designated pedestrian links around Roxas Boulevard and the stations instead of crossing directly toward a nearby map pin. Steps and ground surfaces may be slippery in rain. Check train hours, lift availability and fares for the day. Night photographs and older descriptions of 24-hour opening do not establish that every gate and facility remains accessible overnight. Shorten the visit if access controls or service preparations require it.

Treat the shrine’s small facilities as parts of one visit rather than counting them as separate destinations. The links below are places with different purposes, not a fixed same-day timetable or a walking route. Allow separate rail or road travel time, and on busy Wednesdays consider finishing after the shrine and a meal.
Consider a separate road transfer for shopping or an indoor break. Check the actual connection from the shrine and your onward route.
For a further history and park visit in Manila, match your station to the intended park entrance and check its own access rules and outdoor conditions.
